title: Ironbridge Pharma — inference onboarding jotter
content:
Quick capture from 2026-03-09 call with Ironbridge R&D + infra (informal / messy). Purpose: capture asks, gotchas, next steps for a Private/VPC deployment tailored to regulated drug-discovery workflows.

Participants:
- Evan Morales (Redwood CS)
- Priya Shah (Redwood Solutions)
- Marco Alvarez (Redwood SRE on-call)
- Dr. Lian Chen (Ironbridge, Head of ML Ops)
- Samir Patel (Ironbridge, Security)
- Rachel Kim (Ironbridge, Prod infra)

High-level goal:
- Get a Minimal Viable Private deployment for model inference inside Ironbridge AWS account (eu-west-1) that meets data residency, KMS-backed key management, and 99.9% uptime SLAs for batch/interactive experiments. Start with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) + embeddings for similarity search.

Call notes / raw impressions:
- They are extremely sensitive about PHI/chemical IP; default preference is Private (no hosted API).
- Primary workloads: large-batch embedding pipelines (nightly), interactive hypothesis chat for scientists (low-latency), and model evals (automated).
- Target throughput: nightly embeddings ~1.2M documents/day (avg doc length 400 tokens) -> need batching + streaming writes to vector store.
- Interactive SLO: p95 < 300ms for single-turn (most queries ~256 tokens) — they emphasized human-in-the-loop latency.
- Cost sensitivity: procurement will want projected unit costs; focus to recommend quantized weights + batching to reduce token cost.

Technical constraints / requirements noted:
- AWS account owned by customer (Mandate: deploy in their VPC, private subnets, NAT egress control).
- KMS integration: must support AWS KMS and optionally HSM for signing keys; audit logs to be exported to their central Splunk/S3.
- Private control plane model: they prefer Redwood Private with customer-managed infra.
- Data flow: inputs + conversation history must never leave eu-west-1. No backups to public S3 outside region.
- Vector DB: they currently use managed Redis / RedisGears for fast lookup; we should validate our embedding output shape and dtype.
- Model artifacts: they will start with a 13B dense model (cost/latency balance) and may test 70B on dedicated pools later.
- Network egress: security team wants a list of endpoints that Redwood Private control plane will call (for updates/metrics) — ideally allowlist minimal set or provide air-gap option.

Gotchas / risks called out:
- Hidden token blow-ups when combining long contexts + generated outputs -> need integrated token accounting in demo.
- Nightly embed pipeline: high concurrency + long sequences may trigger OOM on default instance types; recommend explicit batch sizing and sharding.
- KMS rotation cadence — their infosec wants auto-rotate every 90 days; ensure Redwood Private supports rotation without service disruption and key-id mapping in logs.
- Audit trail: they will require per-request provenance (which model version, quantization profile, prompt template) for regulated audits. Need to prove RBAC and immutable logs.
- Model fallback behavior: must not silently switch to lower-capacity model without explicit notices for experiments.

Preliminary model / infra suggestions (brain dump):
- Start: redwood-verified 13B (quantized int8 or int8+kv) with dedicated pool of 4x A10G (or equivalent) for interactive SLOs; autoscale policy: keep baseline of 2 nodes, scale to 8 for daytime bursts.
- Embeddings: batched pipeline using Redwood batch API, chunk docs to 512 tokens, use streaming write to Redis vector store; measure throughput at 200k docs/hour and tune batch size.
- Caching: enable prefix/KV cache for interactive use to save on repeated context.
- Canary rollout: route 10% of scientist traffic to new model, collect quality metrics via eval harness (we should provide template prompt sets).

Open questions to clarify with them:
- Exact SLA/uptime they need for Private control plane vs inference nodes (they said 99.9% for inference, unsure about control plane).
- Does their procurement allow vendor-managed images (AMI) in account or do they require building from a fixed compliance image?
- Are there approved HSM vendors (AWS CloudHSM vs external) they must use?
- Which vector store telemetry is acceptable to export (they prefer no document-level payloads in logs).

Short-term next steps (owner / due):
- Action: Provide a 3-slide technical summary (network endpoints, required instance types, KMS rotation behavior) for Security review. Owner: Evan. Due: 2026-03-15. (Linked: CS-1978)
- Action: Draft architecture diagram for Private deployment (VPC subnets, NAT, S3 buckets, KMS) + AMI policy options. Owner: Marco. Due: 2026-03-18.
- Action: Provide a cost/back-of-envelope for 13B interactive + nightly embeddings (monthly). Owner: Priya. Due: 2026-03-17.
- Action: Share example eval prompt set (chemistry RAG) and short quality checklist for canary. Owner: Priya + Evan. Due: 2026-03-20.
- Action: Confirm allowlistable outbound endpoints & offline/air-gapped deployment feasibility. Owner: Samir (Ironbridge) + Marco. Due: 2026-03-22.

Longer-term items:
- Plan dedicated 70B test nodes if 13B fails quality bar for specific assays.
- Integration playbook for Redis vector store (schemata, normalization, vector dimensionality).
- Run a 2-week pilot with 10 scientists, measure latency, hallucination rate, token cost per query.

Notes to self (things to remember when prepping docs):
- Keep wording conservative around PHI; call out immutable audit logs in the architecture piece.
- Provide both managed and fully air-gapped options — they'll ask procurement.
- Pull prior notes from Confluence page: /display/Ironbridge+Onboarding (linked above) and reference CS-1978 for ticket history.

Random quick jots:
- Bring up quantization tradeoffs during 2nd call: int8 vs 4-bit + perf numbers.
- Make a short demo that shows token accounting across convo + generation so security can see cost/volume.
- Check if RedisGears allows us to stream batched similarity results efficiently (Marco to validate).

End of jotter — will iterate into a cleaned onboarding brief after follow-ups.
